data.description:
## The failure

Scheduled Test Suite run `33950878570` (2026-09-05 06:49 UTC, `headSha a33333b8709a`) failed
THREE sweep lanes — `sweep (macos, full suite)`, `sweep (py3.15)`, `sweep (py3.14t)` — all with the
IDENTICAL failure:

```
FAILED tests/interfaces/store/test_reconciler_apply_bindings.py::
       test_reconcile_once_threads_composed_runtime_transport_into_apply
>       assert recorded.get("client") is captured_transport, (
E       AssertionError: the apply phase must forward the composed runtime's transport as client=
E       assert None is namespace(name='composed-transport')
```

`sweep (windows)` also failed but is `continue-on-error` by design and belongs to the Windows
support-target epic; it is not part of this ticket.

## This is a DIFFERENT cause from the gating-cell failure

Filed as distinct from bug `ac93-09f5-6004-44af` (`naval-halfasleep-shorebird`), which is the
gating `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.13)` failure in
`tests/unit/workflow/test_terraform_code_review_tools.py`. Evidence they are separate:

- Different test, different file, different subsystem (reconciler runtime/transport threading vs
  Terraform grounding session routing).
- Different assertion and different failure mode.
- `ac93` is PROBABILISTIC (a CPython `id()`-recycling flake, reproduced at roughly 12% locally).
  This one is DETERMINISTIC: it hit 3 of 3 sweep lanes with a byte-identical assertion, which a
  ~12% flake would not do.
- The gating py3.13 cell did NOT fail on this test in the same run, and the sweep lanes did NOT
  fail on the Terraform test.

## What is established so far

- `test_reconcile_once_threads_composed_runtime_transport_into_apply` PASSES in isolation on
  current `origin/main` (`c01992039092`), and passes when the whole file
  `tests/interfaces/store/test_reconciler_apply_bindings.py` is run alone.
- It is therefore ORDER- or SELECTION-dependent: it manifests only under the broader run the
  sweep lanes perform, not under a narrow selection.
- The two commits that landed after the failing `headSha a33333b8709a` (`469d199aa0a7`,
  `c01992039092`) touch neither the reconciler nor this test, so the defect is still live on
  `origin/main` — it is not already fixed.
- Pairing the test with `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_internal_shim_removal.py` (added by
  `a33333b8709a`, "Remove reconciler internal shims") does NOT reproduce it; that specific pairing
  is refuted as the trigger.

## Leading hypothesis (NOT yet confirmed)

The test loads engine modules by synthetic name via a local `_load` helper that writes into
`sys.modules`:

```python
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
mod = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
sys.modules[name] = mod
```

It then monkeypatches `runtime.compose_reconciler_runtime` on the module object IT loaded. Many
other test files load the same synthetic `rebar_reconciler.*` names. If an earlier test leaves a
different module object registered under one of those names — or if production `reconcile.py`
resolves its own copy of `runtime` rather than the one the test patched — the stub never applies,
the real runtime composes, and `client` arrives as `None`. That is exactly the observed
`assert None is namespace(name='composed-transport')`.

This is a hypothesis consistent with all evidence so far; it has NOT been confirmed by
bisecting the polluting test. Confirm it before fixing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failure is REPRODUCED locally under a run selection that triggers it, and the specific
      polluting test (or the module-identity mechanism) is named with evidence.
- [ ] The root cause is confirmed — not merely consistent with the hypothesis above.
- [ ] The fix addresses the cause on its merits. If the defect is cross-test `sys.modules`
      pollution, fix the isolation (the class), not just this one assertion; do not reorder tests
      or relax the assertion to make it pass.
- [ ] `sweep (macos, full suite)`, `sweep (py3.15)` and `sweep (py3.14t)` pass on `main`.
- [ ] `sweep (windows)` is explicitly OUT of scope here (continue-on-error, Windows epic).
data.title: Three sweep lanes RED on test_reconcile_once_threads_composed_runtime_transport_into_apply: apply gets client=None under full-suite ordering
